To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the model ensemble reproduced the FACE and chamber experimental results well, 2) modelled leaf area is the key source of variation among rice crop models in predicting yield response to E-[C02], and 3) the uncertainty will be reduced by improving models to account for E-[CO2 × N] interactions.
the uncertainty in crop models in predicting crop yield under elevated [CO2], in this case rice yield, is associated with morphological responses of rice to elevated [CO]2.

the uncertainty in the rice model predictions of yield enhancement in response to elevated CO2 was associated with the models' predictions of leaf area, which is the key factor that controls the photosynthetic carbon gain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the causes of uncertainty in crop model predictions of rice yield response to E-[[CO2]].
the causes of variation in the rice models and how to reduce the variation to make the model more useful in future yield forecasts.
the uncertainty of rice model predictions of yield response to E-[Co2] and the causes of the variation among models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
models that overestimate leaf area in the absence of elevated CO2 tend to overestimate yield response to elevated CO2.

the variation of the modelled yield responses to E-[CO 2 ] was not associated with the photosynthetic response of the modelled crop, but was significantly associated to the predictions of leaf development.

the variation among the models is associated with the prediction of morphological development and that the variation can be reduced by incorporating conservative nature of the development into the models.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

models that over-predicted yield in one experiment tended to over-predict in other experiments, and this was not associated with the magnitude of photosynthesis response to E-[[CO2]], but was associated with the prediction of the effect of E-[CO₂] on leaf area.
the model ensemble can predict the rice response to E-[Co2] well, and model uncertainty is associated with leaf area.

the modelled secondary effects on morphological development were the sources of model variation, and the conservative nature of morphological response to [CO2] should be considered to reduce uncertainty.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the variation among models can be reduced by incorporating a conservative nature of morphological development in response to E[CO2] into rice models.
coordinated efforts to evaluate crop models with experimental data will help to reduce the uncertainty in model predictions of the effects of E-[ CO2] on rice yield.
model uncertainty can be reduced by improving the representation of the morphological development response to E-[ CO2] and the interactions between E-[ CO2], nitrogen and other factors.
